title: Finite Q3 split-step Gibbs stationarity and KMS boundary residual
question: For the actual finite-Q3 onsite-plus-all-bond Lie--Trotter products, does the finite Gibbs stationarity defect and the analytic KMS boundary defect decrease under mesh refinement for both term orders, time signs, beta values and the path4/path6 exhaustion pair?

model.real_split: S_{delta,order}(t)=prod_k exp(-i delta H_k/hbar) in each registered order, repeated N=t/delta times
model.gibbs_state: rho_beta=exp(-beta H)/Tr(exp(-beta H)) for the same finite H
model.kms_boundary: R=Tr(rho A alpha^S_t(B))-Tr(rho alpha^S_{t+i beta hbar}(B) A), with complex split inverse constructed in reverse factor order
model.exact_control: The exact H orbit has stationarity defect and KMS residual zero up to floating-point tolerance.

adversarial_review.check: With alpha_t(X)=exp(-iHt/hbar) X exp(iHt/hbar), the finite KMS boundary is evaluated at t+i beta hbar; the manifest hbar=1 convention is explicit and the exact control is checked.
The inverse of the complex product is built from reversed factor order and -z; it is not replaced by a Hermitian adjoint outside the real axis.
Every row uses the Gibbs state of the same exact H that defines the reference orbit; the split product is not falsely treated as its generator.
Only oscillator dimension 3 is admitted; a dimension-2 control that makes the registered terms commute is excluded from the result.
Coarse/fine residuals are reported and checked as a finite diagnostic; a two-point decrease is not promoted to a uniform Trotter rate.
Both path4/path6, both registered term orders and both real-time signs are retained; path6 is a finite structured exhaustion member only.
The independent lane reconstructs the oscillator, Hamiltonian, Gibbs state, real/complex products and trace residuals without importing the primary module.
Lean R247 checks the exact finite Gibbs normalization/commutation fixture; Python carries the noncommuting 3-level matrices and KMS residual.
No volume/source/cutoff-uniform common core, all-shape Cauchy theorem, common alpha, OS/KMS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A follows.

lean_crosscheck.role: R247 checks the exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation and the conditional-transfer scope; Python checks the actual 3-level Q3 split and KMS matrices.

qft_interface.closed: For each finite path4/path6 member, exact-H Gibbs control is KMS-stationary, while the noncommuting split products have explicitly measured stationarity and analytic KMS boundary residuals that decrease on the declared two-point mesh in both orders and signs.
qft_interface.open: The finite trend does not supply a volume-, source-, cutoff- or beta-uniform rate, a common unbounded core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion independence, one common alpha, or a Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS quotient.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the measured KMS/stationarity residual as a finite compatibility check while attacking the missing uniform direct-D/delta-D history estimate and common-core exhaustion theorem; do not promote the two-point mesh trend.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 Q3 KMS diagnostic. It is not a thermodynamic-limit KMS theorem, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, or a QFT/Clay result.
no_overclaim: A finite split product approaching the exact Gibbs KMS orbit on path4/path6 does not identify the two OS phases with one thermodynamic Q3 dynamics and does not close any downstream physical gate.
